etymologies.heading: Etymology
paragraphs: From Middle English bridel, from Old English brīdel, from Proto-West Germanic *brigdil, from Proto-Germanic *brigdilaz (“strap, rein”), equivalent to braid +‎ -le.
senses: (equestrianism) The headgear with which a horse is directed and which carries a bit and reins.
(transitive) To check, restrain, or control with, or as if with, a bridle; as in bridle your tongue.
